## TL;DR

The Work Queue now has independent **Human** and **Held** show/hide toggles in
the header, between the **Client board** link and the empty-columns `><` button.
Hiding a category removes exactly the tasks its bottom-left parked list contains
from the board columns; showing it restores them. The bottom-left controls were
reordered to **Human, Held, Archived**, and both the toggle row and its expanded
rows follow that order. The choice persists in `localStorage`, defaults to
visible, and does not change task status or assignment semantics.

## Work and rationale

I kept the filtering in `WorkView.vue` rather than in the shared repo store.
`repo.byStatus()` feeds the Pipeline view, dashboard, keyboard navigation and
board collapse helpers, so changing it would have made this Work Queue preference
leak into unrelated pages. Instead the view derives a `hiddenTaskIds` set from
the store's existing `humanTasks` and `heldTasks` computeds and exposes a
`visibleByStatus(status)` helper. `BoardColumn` gained an optional `tasks` prop;
when supplied it uses that list for rendering, the column count, and the
empty-column message, and when omitted it falls back to `repo.byStatus()` as
before. That keeps every other BoardColumn consumer unchanged while making the
column's count agree with what is actually on screen.

Membership deliberately mirrors the parked lists: `humanTasks` excludes done and
archived tasks, and `heldTasks` uses the tag- and expiry-aware active-hold test.
The task description links the new controls to "those task groups" exposed by
the bottom-left controls, so hiding Human should remove the same rows a user
would see in the Human list. A task that is both human-assigned and held needs to
be visible in both categories to remain on the board.

The header controls reuse the existing Pipeline/Board `.view-toggle` container
and its 28px inner-button metrics, so they sit alongside the existing Work Queue
controls instead of introducing a new visual language. Their buttons use a
separate `.queue-visibility-btn` class whose CSS is declared alongside
`.view-toggle-btn`, which keeps styling shared without making every future
`.view-toggle-btn` query also match the category filters. Each button is a native
`<button>` with `aria-pressed` for state, an action-oriented `aria-label`
("Hide human-assigned tasks" / "Show human-assigned tasks"), and a visible
`Eye`/`EyeOff` glyph plus the category name. Keyboard operation is native and I
added a visible `:focus-visible` outline.

I also made two adjacent behaviours respect the visible list. The single-status
`?status=` chip count now uses `visibleByStatus`, and the bulk `><` control
considers filtered columns empty, so hiding the last visible card in a column
allows "collapse empty columns" to work on what the user actually sees.
Keyboard navigation already builds its flat list from `visibleTasks`, so I
switched that to the filtered helper as well. Hidden tasks cannot be keyboard-
focused or dragged, which follows from them not being rendered.

The bottom-left toggle order and the expanded row order were both changed to
Human, Held, Archived. The settings are independent and persist under
`repoos.work.humanVisible` and `repoos.work.heldVisible`, defaulting to visible
so the board looks unchanged for anyone who never touches them. The parked lists
themselves are untouched, so human, held and archived tasks remain reachable in
one click even when hidden from the columns.

Focused coverage lives in `src/ui-app/tests/work-queue-visibility.test.ts`. It
checks the header placement order, each filter in isolation, restoring a filter,
independence when both are hidden, persistence across a remount, the reordered
bottom-left controls, the filtered single-status count, and that `BoardColumn`
counts the list it is given rather than the store's full list. I also updated
`user-docs/concepts.md` to document the new toggles and the parked-list order.

## Approaches tried

My first version reused the `.view-toggle-btn` class directly for the new
buttons. That was visually perfect but changed the meaning of a generic selector:
`pipeline-view.test.ts` asserts that every `.view-toggle-btn` on `/work` is
Pipeline or Board, and the scoped check caught the two extra buttons. I fixed the
whole class of problem rather than just that assertion by giving the filter
buttons their own class and sharing the CSS through a grouped selector. This
keeps existing view-toggle queries honest and prevents the same collision in
future tests.

I considered adding the filter state to the repo store so `byStatus` could return
filtered lists everywhere. That would have been less plumbing in WorkView, but it
would silently change the Pipeline track, dashboard and collapse helpers, and it
would make the preference global rather than page-local. The `tasks` prop on
`BoardColumn` is a smaller contract and keeps the scope the task asked for.

I also considered filtering by raw `assignee === "human"` and the hold flag
directly, which would include done human tasks. I chose the parked-list
membership instead because the task explicitly ties the header controls to the
bottom-left groups, and it avoids a mismatch between the Human `(n)` count and
what disappears from the board. That rationale is recorded in a code comment so
the next maintainer does not "fix" it into the broader definition accidentally.

## Challenges and blockers

The only failure was the selector collision above. The scoped check's remote
validation runner reported it after the local run; the local rerun of
`pipeline-view.test.ts` and the new visibility suite passed once the classes were
separated. No product or data blockers came up. The preview data is owned by the
server, so I declared shots using the existing `card:humanStep` fixture, which
renders a human-assigned card and therefore also makes the Human parked list
appear.

## Key learnings

- Generic styling classes are also test selectors. Reusing one across a new
  control group can break exact-count/exact-text assertions elsewhere; a shared
  style with a distinct semantic class avoids that.
- Filtering at the page boundary and passing an explicit list down keeps
  page-local preferences from changing shared store behaviour.
- Column counts and empty states must be derived from the same list as the
  rendered cards, or a filter leaves a "0 visible but 2 counted" column.
- When a task describes controls as toggling "those groups", membership should
  match the group's own definition, not a broader interpretation of the label.
